unresolved_distinctions.question: What is the partition of the domain (ISO dates in 2023-2025, n in [0,60]) into input classes on which the truth of the claim could turn — i.e., which calendar behaviors must add_days reproduce (each month-length table entry actually exercised, February in the leap year 2024 vs. non-leap 2023/2025, month rollover at each month boundary, year rollover Dec 31 -> Jan 1, the n=0 identity case, and multi-month spans up to n=60)?
unresolved_distinctions.why_unresolved: The package contains only the implementation source and the claim; no analysis artifact identifying the truth-relevant input classes exists yet, and the claim's quantifier ranges over roughly 67,000 (date, n) pairs that cannot be assessed without a class decomposition.
unresolved_distinctions.required_evidence: A written analysis enumerating the input classes, showing that together they exercise every month-length constant, the leap-year branch for 2024, every month-boundary rollover reachable within n <= 60, and the year-boundary rollover within the 2023-2025 domain.
admissibility_constraints: Per E-A the analysis must identify the classes on which the claim's truth could turn, not merely sample inputs.
The analysis must be recorded as an inspectable artifact so the deterministic root check can confirm coverage of the domain's structural cases.
No authorship or access restriction applies to E-A; any party with the package may produce it.

unresolved_distinctions.question: Over the stated domain, does add_days(d, n) equal the true Gregorian date n days after d for every input (HOLDS), or does some concrete input (d, n) in the domain witness a mismatch (VIOLATED), and if so which one?
unresolved_distinctions.why_unresolved: The claim is asserted, not established: no comparison of add_days output against the true Gregorian calendar has been performed, and no verdict or witness input exists in the package.
unresolved_distinctions.required_evidence: A verdict grounded in comparison against the true Gregorian calendar over the identified input classes; on VIOLATED, one concrete pair ["YYYY-MM-DD", n] inside the domain whose add_days output mechanically differs from the true date n days later.
admissibility_constraints: Per E-C the verdict must come with a concrete violating input on VIOLATED, and the violation must be mechanical: re-running add_days on the cited input and comparing with an independent Gregorian reference must exhibit the mismatch under deterministic root verification.
The cited input must lie inside the stated domain (date in 2023-2025, 0 <= n <= 60).
No authorship restriction applies to E-C; the worker that read the package may produce it.

unresolved_distinctions.question: Has a systematic search for a violating input over the domain been carried out by a party other than the author of the provisional answer (or has such a party argued that no violating input exists in the domain)?
unresolved_distinctions.why_unresolved: No second party has examined the package: the only search that could exist so far would be authored by the same process that formed the provisional verdict, which the task's E-B admissibility condition explicitly excludes.
unresolved_distinctions.required_evidence: A record of a systematic search over the input classes (or a no-violation argument covering the domain), produced by a separately launched process that is not the author of the provisional answer, integrated into the deliverable's evidence.
admissibility_constraints: Per E-B the search or no-violation argument must be 'carried out by a party other than the author of the provisional answer'; a self-audit by the worker that formed the provisional verdict is inadmissible regardless of its quality.
The search must be systematic over the domain (structured by the input classes), not a spot check.
The other party's output must be attributable to a distinct process origin so the authorship separation is verifiable.
